Chromatographic Column.name: C18 silica
Chromatographic Column.reasoning: C18 silica is the primary stationary phase material used inside chromatographic columns for reversed-phase liquid chromatography, essential for the separation function and industry standard.

Chromatographic Column.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Chromatographic Column.reasoning: The column housing is typically made of stainless steel SS316 due to its chemical resistance and mechanical strength, universally used in chromatographic columns.

Chromatographic Column.name: PTFE coating
Chromatographic Column.reasoning: PTFE coatings are commonly applied inside columns or on fittings to provide chemical inertness and reduce sample adsorption, standard in many columns but some alternatives exist.

Chromatographic Column.name: Glass
Chromatographic Column.reasoning: Some columns or parts may include glass components, like frits or viewing windows, but this is less universal hence moderate confidence.

Pump Module.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Pump Module.reasoning: Pump heads, pistons, and valves are generally made from SS316 to withstand high pressure and corrosive solvents; industry standard material.

Pump Module.name: Ceramic
Pump Module.reasoning: Ceramic materials are used for wear-resistant pistons and valve components due to hardness and chemical resistance, commonly used in pump modules.

Pump Module.name: PTFE
Pump Module.reasoning: Seals and diaphragm materials often utilize PTFE for chemical resistance and low friction, widely used in pump module manufacturing.

Pump Module.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Pump Module.reasoning: Some pump module tubing or protective covers may use PET, but not always present, hence moderate confidence.

Autosampler Module.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Autosampler Module.reasoning: Critical structural parts like needles, syringes, and sample loops are often stainless steel SS316 for corrosion resistance and durability.

Autosampler Module.name: PTFE
Autosampler Module.reasoning: Used in tubing and seals for chemical inertness and flexibility; standard for fluidic components in autosamplers.

Autosampler Module.name: Glass
Autosampler Module.reasoning: Glass vials and components may be part of autosampler fluid path but not always integral to all designs, hence moderate confidence.

Autosampler Module.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Autosampler Module.reasoning: Some sample trays or non-fluidic structural parts may use PET, but alternatives exist, resulting in moderate confidence.

Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.name: Silicon
Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.reasoning: Silicon is the fundamental semiconductor material for integrated circuits and essential for any electronics board.

Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.name: Copper
Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.reasoning: Copper is the standard conductor material for PCB traces and internal wiring, universally used in electronics boards.

Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.name: Epoxy resins
Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.reasoning: Used as the matrix in PCB substrates and potting compounds for insulation and mechanical support, standard in electronics.

Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.name: Gold
Acquisition And Control Electronics Boar.reasoning: Gold is often used for pad plating and wire bonding for reliable electrical contacts, common but sometimes alternatives like tin exist.

Degasser Module.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Degasser Module.reasoning: Structural components and gas-permeable membranes support often made from SS316 for corrosion resistance under solvent exposure.

Degasser Module.name: PTFE
Degasser Module.reasoning: Gas-permeable membranes in degassers frequently use PTFE for chemical inertness and gas permeability; standard material.

Degasser Module.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Degasser Module.reasoning: Some tubing and structural parts of degassers can use PET; alternatives exist, so moderate confidence.

Waste And Solvent Management System.name: Polyethylene terephthalate
Waste And Solvent Management System.reasoning: Widely used for solvent-resistant containers and tubing due to chemical inertness; alternatives like HDPE may be used but PET is common.

Waste And Solvent Management System.name: PTFE
Waste And Solvent Management System.reasoning: Seals, tubing liners, and valves often use PTFE for chemical resistance and inertness; essential for solvent management integrity.

Waste And Solvent Management System.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Waste And Solvent Management System.reasoning: Used in pumps or valves within the system for durability and corrosion resistance; common but plastic parts also prevalent.

Column Compartment.name: Aluminum
Column Compartment.reasoning: Housing and structural frame typically use aluminum for lightweight strength and good thermal conductivity.

Column Compartment.name: Stainless steel (SS 316)
Column Compartment.reasoning: Some compartments use stainless steel for durability, but aluminum is more common; hence moderate confidence.

Column Compartment.name: PTFE
Column Compartment.reasoning: Sealing gaskets and tubing inside the compartment frequently use PTFE for chemical resistance; common but replaceable with other polymers.
